stories.title: Tech stocks slide as AI spending worries reignite
stories.summary: U.S. technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday as investors grew more concerned that soaring spending on artificial intelligence will prove unsustainable, with the Nasdaq Composite sliding 694 points, or 2.6%, its biggest drop since June. Meta fell 7% after disclosing billions of dollars in additional future spending commitments and missing profit expectations despite soaring revenue. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang added to the unease by saying the industry lacks the capital needed to fuel growth of so-called neoclouds, while shares of SpaceX, Nvidia and CoreWeave also slid.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico privacy case
stories.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion on Wednesday after a jury found the company misled consumers about data privacy, in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica obtained data from millions of Facebook users without consent. The judge wrote that Facebook's wrongdoing went to the heart of its core business practices, and found a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted under state law before reducing it to $25 billion. Meta's chief legal officer said the company is confident it will prevail on appeal.

stories.title: AI-found PHP flaws force dozens of government sites offline
stories.summary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities dubbed PHP2Shell, rated 9.2 and found with the help of AI models including GPT and Gemini, have forced 32 UK government services offline and four more into partial disruption as a precaution while patches are applied. Government websites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland and the Netherlands have also been taken offline, and the U.S. NSA has urged organisations to patch or disconnect vulnerable systems. The flaws allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers, and the UK's National Cyber Security Centre warned organisations to patch immediately or consider going offline until fixed.

stories.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 models arrive on Google Cloud
stories.summary: OpenAI announced on October 21 that its frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden, so enterprises can use them where they already build and pay through Google Cloud Marketplace. The initial lineup is GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, rolling out now in private preview to select enterprise customers, with general availability expected in the coming weeks. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the company is focused on giving customers a broad selection of models, and the models are also slated for Google's Antigravity coding tool and Gemini Agent.

stories.title: Apple adds AI features to Pages, Keynote and Numbers
stories.summary: Apple's iWork apps have added new Intelligent Assistant features for Apple Creator Studio subscribers, according to release notes reported on October 22. In Pages the assistant can start a first draft, adjust tone and generate images and shapes from natural language; Keynote can generate slides, presenter notes and images; and Numbers can uncover insights, build complex formulas and suggest charts. Keynote also gains a new Interchange Format (.keyx) for importing and exporting presentations more easily in other apps.

stories.title: Ethics complaint filed over suspected AI image in Wisconsin race
stories.summary: An Eau Claire resident filed a complaint with the Wisconsin Ethics Commission over U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden's use of a potentially AI-generated image of opponent Rebecca Cooke in an advertisement for their October 20 debate. The photo, circulated ahead of the debate on X by @TeamVanOrden, shows Cooke appearing to scowl deeply, and Cooke's campaign contends it was generated rather than a real photo. Van Orden's spokeswoman called the complaint a cheap publicity stunt filed three months too late, after a cease-and-desist letter sent September 30 over an earlier video.
